sections.content: How many people are "metal working production and maintenance fitters"?

181,210 people

were counted on the census as "metal working production and maintenance fitters" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Metal working production and maintenance fitters erect, install and repair electrical and mechanical plant and industrial machinery, fit and assemble parts and sub-assemblies in the manufacture of metal products, and test and adjust new motor vehicles and engines.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "metal working production and maintenance fitters" there were more men than women (97.3% compared with 2.7%).

This means "metal working production and maintenance fitters" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled metal, electrical and electronic trades".

Men made up 97.3% and women made up 2.7% of "metal working production and maintenance fitters"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "metal working production and maintenance fitters" included:

  • fork-lift truck drivers
  • tool makers, tool fitters and markers-out
  • elementary construction occupations (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "metal working production and maintenance fitters" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "metal working production and maintenance fitters", 12.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "metal working production and maintenance fitters" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "metal working production and maintenance fitters" included:

  • metal working machine operatives
  • other administrative occupations
  • delivery drivers and couriers

We can look at who worked as "metal working production and maintenance fitters" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of men than women with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "metal working production and maintenance fitters" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "metal working production and maintenance fitters", 8.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (91.3% compared with 8.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (86.6%) than self-employed (13.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
